consequences: A new file needs the header. CI's lint step needs pipx, which GitHub's Ubuntu runners have. The bundle's legal comment now names the GPL.
context: The code was MIT with a five-line header per file, and only oxlint ran; the sister project two-edged-sword had moved to GPL with a two-line SPDX header and a formatter.
decision: LICENSE is the verbatim GPL v3 text and the image/whistle carve-out moved to NOTICE. Every source file starts with the two-line copyright and SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later header, as do the generated exercise tables (their generators write it). npm run lint is prettier --check, oxlint --deny-warnings and Ruff (via pipx) over scripts/; Prettier is semi-free, single-quoted, 100 columns, matching the code as it was; Ruff likewise single-quoted at 100.
title: Relicensed GPL-3.0-or-later; Prettier, oxlint and Ruff gate lint

consequences: useSpokenCues takes the setting; the beep is fired from the tick like the voice, not pre-scheduled. Mute still silences everything.
context: The spoken 'ten seconds left' bothered a training partner, but the countdown beeps, whistle and bell were still wanted.
decision: A persisted three-way setting (voice, double beep, nothing), defaulting to voice, picked from a stopwatch menu beside Sound on the run screen. The double beep is a fifth above the countdown beep so it cannot read as the countdown starting early.
title: Ten-second warning is its own setting, not part of mute

consequences: The spoken line follows the on-screen name, not the next step, so the announcement over cardio names the machine. Speech for a get-ready lands about 0.9s after its bell; a routine opening on a get-ready folds it into Let's go.
context: Wanted the get-ready to announce the exercise. Active-recovery routines run 'Get ready: X', a cardio minute, then a bare 'Get ready' into X.
decision: A 'Get ready: X' step says 'Get ready for X' with the step's load; a bare 'Get ready' names the next exercise unless the previous get-ready already said the same with nothing of X in between; any other get-ready name (Change Sides) is said as written. Switched by a speech-bubble button beside the ten-second warning, persisted, on by default. The full-screen button was removed, since opening a routine goes full screen; F still toggles it.
title: Get-readys speak what they are for, once
